clue.text: Measures widely adopted using rhythm method

parts.note: as a noun, metric is the metrical pattern or rhythm of verse
a system is a method or orderly way of doing things

explanation.surface: A sly line about family planning: contraception by the rhythm method being widely adopted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measures widely adopted' and 'rhythm method' both suggest birth control; the first is really the definition, the second gives the two words in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal set of units of length, mass and volume is used across most of the world.

clue.text: Calling for online mission?

parts.note: E- as a prefix means electronic or online, as in email
a vocation is a sense of mission or calling in life

explanation.surface: A recruitment line asking whether anyone is answering the call for an internet task.
explanation.definitionFit: An evocation is a summoning or calling up, as of spirits or memories.

clue.text: Director often wants one to get back

definitions.meaning: a film director frequently asks for a scene to be shot again

explanation.surface: A film director keen on a repeat shot to win something back.
explanation.definitionFit: A second shooting of a scene, and as a verb, to recapture something lost.

clue.text: Theatrical make-up fellow dismissed by agent

definitions.note: as a noun, a theatrical is a professional stage performer

parts.note: a person's make-up is their nature or character

indicators.note: the fellow is sent away from the agent's word, leaving the rest

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another

explanation.surface: An actor in heavy stage make-up gets dropped by their agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a stage performer; the agent is a FACTOR, which loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who specialises in distinctive supporting roles is one kind of stage professional.

clue.text: Crucible's top puzzle controlled by the government

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: A riddle about the Crucible theatre's leading puzzle being state-run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' looks like a noun but is a verb: rearrange the twelve letters of CRUCIBLESTOP. The Crucible is a Sheffield theatre, home of snooker's world championship.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the economy run by the state, as opposed to private business.

clue.text: Cheap wine put new heart into board

indicators.note: the middle letter of the board's word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a plank is a long board of timber

explanation.surface: Someone revives a drooping committee board with cheap wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put new heart into' sounds like encouragement; it replaces the central A of PLANK with O.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for inexpensive, inferior table wine.

clue.text: A drop of dew in finest fresh flower

indicators.note: the dropped letter goes inside the word for finest

parts.note: best means finest

indicators.note: just a single drop, the first letter, of the word dew

parts.note: raw means fresh, uncooked

explanation.surface: A dewdrop glistening on the loveliest newly opened bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedstraw is a wild plant of the genus Galium with small clustered blooms.

clue.text: Idol from Nutmeg's generation

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter, so Nutmeg's means 'Nutmeg is', I'M
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: A pop idol produced by the setter's own generation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a graven likeness worshipped as a god, a carved representation.

clue.text: State thanks soldiers from the East infiltrating spies

indicators.note: the turned pair gets inside the spies' letters

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A country grateful as troops from the East penetrate a spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a Balkan nation, an independent country on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Men at last striking right attitude for one paving the way?

indicators.note: striking out removes the letter from the shoemakers' word

parts.note: cobblers are shoemakers, who work at a last, the foot-shaped form
tone means attitude, as in the tone of a letter

explanation.surface: Workers finally on strike over the right stance on paving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men at last' looks like 'men at the end'; a last is a shoemaker's form, so these men are COBBLERS, which loses an R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded stone set with others to make a road surface, so it literally paves a way.

clue.text: Game lady never joined

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players avoid holding the unmatched queen
a woman who has never married, never joined in wedlock

explanation.surface: A sporting woman who never signed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a children's card game and an old term for a spinster who never wed.

clue.text: Recording agent initially calm during any difference of opinion

parts.note: a disc is a sound recording
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

indicators.note: the letter sits within the word any
only the opening letter of calm is used

explanation.surface: A record company's agent stays calm through any disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A discrepancy is a disagreement or inconsistency between accounts or views.

clue.text: Illicit dealers want to trade in pints, perhaps

indicators.note: the two words go inside the word for pints

parts.note: pints are an example of beers
to want is to lack
market can mean trade, commerce

explanation.surface: Smugglers keen to deal in beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want to trade' reads as desire to do business, but 'want' is a noun-like lack and 'trade' a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Those running an illegal trade in scarce or controlled goods.

clue.text: In absence of leader, Frank remained

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for frank is missing

parts.note: plain means frank, candid

explanation.surface: With the boss away, Frank stayed put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles of verbs of staying: had lain means had stayed lying there.

clue.text: Casting director, plastered, finds a way to get up

indicators.note: casting can mean throwing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken film director in the middle of casting still finds a way to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting director' looks like a job title; 'Casting' is the anagram signal and 'director' only gives D, to mix with PLASTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding set of steps is a means of climbing to reach high places.

clue.text: Final strains in furious duel between Poles

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit between parts of the poles' word

parts.note: posts are poles, upright stakes

indicators.note: a furious duel is wild, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Closing music sounding over a fierce fight between Polish rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland or magnetic poles; here it means upright stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Postludes are closing pieces of music played at the end of a service or work.

clue.text: Refresh last of those in party with invitation to get up

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the word for party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word those is used

parts.note: 'Do rise!' is a polite invitation to stand

explanation.surface: Someone at a party is invited to stand up and freshen up.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a bad smell is to make a room or garment smell fresh again.

clue.text: With two good men around, henchman's most decorous

indicators.note: the two saints are placed either side of the henchman
two good men means the saint abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
an aide is a henchman or assistant; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A gangster's sidekick, flanked by two saints, is on his best behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sober and respectable, so the superlative is the most proper.

clue.text: Winger's shorts hung awkwardly

definitions.note: a winger is a bird, a winged creature; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: hung awkwardly suggests disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football winger's shorts hang badly on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer playing on the flank; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European songbird, a creature with wings, speckled brown and famous for its repeated phrases.

clue.text: Commander heading for capital in revolution

parts.note: CO is commanding officer, a commander
going up is the British idiom for travelling to London or a capital

explanation.surface: A military leader marching on the capital in a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' is not a first-letter signal: in Britain you go up to London, and up trains run towards the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden seizure of power, an overthrow of government.

clue.text: Considers speaker's customs

indicators.note: as voiced by a speaker, the word sounds like another

parts.note: ways are customs or habits

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about the customs of a public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh a matter is to ponder or deliberate on it.

clue.text: Having made the side, a sportsman's idle very rarely

parts.note: once in means having got into the team
a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport; the 's stands for 'is'
to moon about is to idle

explanation.surface: Once selected, a sportsman slacks off, but only rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson who has played for the university against its rival.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something happening only on the rarest of occasions.

clue.text: First bit of chapped skin? Tear off a strip

indicators.note: only the opening letter of chapped is used

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: Peeling chapped skin, and someone ripping a piece off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear off a strip' looks like peeling skin; it is the British idiom 'tear a strip off', to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear a strip off someone is British slang for telling them off sharply, to scold.

clue.text: See 4
Demanding chap behind English team

indicators.note: the chap comes after the English team

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A pushy man trailing the England side.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or urgent, making heavy demands.

clue.text: Honour daughter, mean son having scarpered

indicators.note: scarpered means run off, so the son's letter leaves the word

parts.note: to signify is to mean

explanation.surface: Praise your daughter, now that your stingy son has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective, stingy; it is the verb, SIGNIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To dignify is to give distinction or honour to someone.
